options.text: The product is the label rectangle area, with no link to the shaded fraction.
The shaded piece is $\frac{1}{15}$ of the unit square.
$\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{1}{5}$ equals the area of the shaded rectangle inside the unit square.
The same shading finds the perimeter of the unit square.

stem:
Qasim shades a unit square. He takes $\frac{1}{3}$ of the square and then $\frac{1}{5}$ of that third to show $\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{1}{5}$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims are correct?

teacher.key_rationale: One fifth of one third of the unit square is 1/15 of the unit square, and that shaded area is the product. Stopping at the rectangle-area label or reading perimeter from the shading both miss the area-product link.
